content_groups.group_title: Q: Is oedema diagnostic of pre-eclampsia?

blocks.text: No. Mild dependent oedema can occur physiologically in pregnancy. Pre-eclampsia is diagnosed based on hypertension with proteinuria and/or evidence of maternal organ dysfunction, depending on the diagnostic framework being used.
Hypertension is a key feature of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, including pre-eclampsia.

content_groups.group_title: Q: What BP is considered hypertension in pregnancy?

blocks.text: A blood pressure of **140/90 mmHg or higher**, appropriately confirmed according to the clinical context.

content_groups.group_title: Q: What neurological signs might you look for?

items.text: Altered neurological state where severe disease is suspected

blocks.text: It indicates neuromuscular irritability and, in the appropriate setting, can support concern for severe pre-eclampsia.

blocks.text: BP, pulse, RR, temperature, SpO₂ where indicated.
Bilateral vs unilateral, pitting, warmth, tenderness, asymmetry.

**“I would assess maternal and fetal wellbeing and investigate for pre-eclampsia, DVT or systemic causes according to the findings.”**
